dropped_candidates.role: Alleged Chief Fiscal Officer, Municipality of Anchorage
dropped_candidates.decision_summary: Selected Tyler Technologies enterprise Payments platform for MOA, May 26, 2026
dropped_candidates.reason: Gate 1 (Named Subject): The MOA's own institutional Finance Department page names Philippe D. Brice as the current Chief Fiscal Officer, not Lance Wilber. No independently fetchable institutional source — no MOA leadership page, no mayoral press release, no MOA staff directory — confirms Wilber holds the CFO role. The only sources naming Wilber as CFO are the Tyler Technologies BusinessWire press release and its downstream reprints (GovTech, Must Read Alaska, StockTitan). Gate 1 fails. Gate 3 (Decision Consequential): The Anchorage contract is for Tyler's enterprise Payments platform — a cloud-based billing and collections system. No AI component is named in the Anchorage contract. AI is referenced only in relation to Tyler's general corporate roadmap, not the Anchorage deal itself. Inferential chain (Tyler pursues AI products, therefore this contract eventually touches AI) is explicitly prohibited as equivalent to the GCI/Quintillion fiber-enables-AI pattern. Gate 3 fails. Gate 4 (Multi-Source Corroboration): Must Read Alaska is an explicit BusinessWire press release reprint. StockTitan is a press release aggregation service. GovTech draws from the same BusinessWire announcement. All three named corroborators are downstream of the single Tyler Technologies press release — one source amplified, not independent corroboration. Gate 4 fails.

dropped_candidates.decision_summary: Co-authored 'Artificial intelligence/machine learning in Alaska Native healthcare systems: symposium perspectives,' International Journal of Circumpolar Health, published May 23, 2026
dropped_candidates.reason: Gate 2 (Recent Decision): Primary source (Tandfonline DOI 10.1080/22423982.2026.2677426) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden. Paper title and Epub date confirmed via PubMed (PMID 42176020), but decision content and Hiratsuka's specific authorship cannot be confirmed from a live fetchable page. Gate 2 conditionally fails on unconfirmable primary-source content. Gate 3 (Decision Consequential): A journal publication documenting symposium perspectives does not constitute a binary decision (approve/block, fund/cut, launch/halt). The paper records what 31 symposium participants discussed in 2025; it does not commit a named actor to a specific operational action with a concrete enforcement mechanism confirmable from a fetchable page. Gate 3 fails. Gate 4 (Multi-Source Corroboration): The cited corroborator (PMC12009764) is confirmed by fetch to be a different 2025 paper (Brian Travis Rice et al., 'Community-engaged artificial intelligence') — not the Hiratsuka 2026 symposium paper. The 2025 paper confirms the consortium but does not corroborate the specific 2026 paper or Hiratsuka's decision ownership in it. No second independently fetchable source for the specific 2026 paper was located. Gate 4 fails.

_validation_note: Both candidates presented to the validator fail multiple gates at the 30-day window. Broadening to 45 days (to May 4, 2026) was considered but yields no additional candidates: the scouts' only other surfaced candidate (Troy Goldie/GCI/Databricks, March 16, 2026) falls 94 days before the run date, well outside even the 45-day broadened window. The 45-day broadening was therefore not executed. Candidate 1 (Wilber/Tyler): Fails Gate 1 — MOA Finance Department page names Philippe D. Brice as CFO, not Wilber; no independently fetchable institutional source resolves this. Fails Gate 3 — no AI component in the Anchorage contract. Fails Gate 4 — all three corroborators are downstream reprints of one BusinessWire press release. Candidate 2 (Hiratsuka/symposium paper): Fails Gate 2 — primary source paywalled (HTTP 403); decision content unconfirmable. Fails Gate 3 — symposium perspectives paper is not a binary operational decision. Fails Gate 4 — cited corroborator is a different 2025 paper, not the 2026 Hiratsuka paper. This is an honest no-target cycle. The Anchorage AI primary-source pool is thin for the May 19 to June 18 window; both candidates surface real actors and real events but neither meets the bar for consequential, independently corroborated, AI-specific binary decisions owned by a named Anchorage-bowl subject.
